title: Wendelin: fiducia as persuasion we are counted just — required beyond general assent
source_text: LV. Alii tamen Scholae Reformatae Theologi aliter explicant fiduciam istam, quam dicunt esse proprium & specificum actum fidei justificantis: nempe docent eam esse persuasionem qua fideles singuli certo apud se statuunt, se propter Christi meritum Deo gratos & acceptos esse, sibiique donatam esse salutem & vitam aeternam. Sic Wendelinus explicat fiduciam quam fidei tribuit. Fiducia, inquit, est tertia & principalis pars fidei justificantis, qua generales Evangelii promissiones nobis applicamus, & nos propter Christi meritum justos a Deo reputari, aeternaeque vitae haeredes fore, plane persuasum habemus. Lib. 1. cap. 24. Thesi 15. Et in Explicatione addit, Respectu fiduciae hujus fides appellatur salvifica & justificans. Neminem enim justificat Deus, nisi qui fiduciam in Christo collocat, & propter ejus meritum sibi peccata remitti firmiter credit. Itaque ad salutem non sufficit notitia mysteriorum divinorum, vel assensus etiam generalis; sed necessario requiritur quoque fiducia.
pass_a_gloss: Yet other Theologians of the Reformed School explain that trust which they say is the proper and specific act of justifying faith otherwise: namely they teach that it is a persuasion by which each of the faithful certainly lays down with himself that for Christ's merit he is grateful and acceptable to God, and that salvation and eternal life have been given to him. Thus Wendelin explains the trust which he attributes to faith. Trust, he says, is the third and principal part of justifying faith, by which we apply to ourselves the general promises of the Gospel, and have it plainly persuaded that for Christ's merit we are reputed just by God, and shall be heirs of eternal life. Book 1, chapter 24, Thesis 15. And in the Explanation he adds, With respect to this trust faith is called saving and justifying. For God justifies no one unless he places trust in Christ, and firmly believes that for His merit sins are remitted to him. And so for salvation knowledge of the divine mysteries, or even general assent, does not suffice; but trust also is necessarily required.
pass_b_english: Other Reformed: proper specific act = persuasion I am accepted and given life for Christ’s merit.
Wendelin: fiducia = third/principal part — apply general Gospel promises; persuaded we are reputed just and heirs.
Respect of this fiducia: faith called saving/justifying.
God justifies none who do not trust in Christ and firmly believe sins remitted for His merit.
Notitia or general assent alone does not suffice.
